situation.text: Hoje você conhece Darius, de Orlando. Alugar bicicleta e capacete.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a falar de um time com We are… e Let’s…, numa partida no ginásio, como o time do Coach e do Slugger.

pages.hook: In many American cities you can rent a bike for an hour or a day, and ride along a lake or a park. Learn the few words you need before you pay and ride away.
pages.polite: Say **I’d like to rent a bike, please.** Ask **Is there a bike lane?** if you want a safe route.

mythfact.why: You usually pay by the hour or by the day.

pages.title: Cultural spotlight
Reading quest — A bike day by the lake
text: Today my friend Darius and I are in **Orlando**. The sky is blue and the day is warm. We see a small shop with many bikes outside. “**Let’s ride!**” says Darius.

Inside, the worker smiles. Darius says, “Hi! **I’d like to rent a bike.**” The worker asks, “**For how long?**” “**For two hours**,” he says. “That’s ten dollars. **Do you want a helmet?**” “**Yes, please.** And a lock.”
Then I ask, “**Is there a bike lane?**” “Yes, **along the lake**,” the worker says. It is a long, flat path, and it is good for beginners. We say thanks and take our bikes.

We ride slowly at first. The lake is beautiful and I see ducks and trees. After one hour, I am **out of breath**. “**Take five**,” I say. We sit on a bench and drink water. “**Wait up!**” says Darius, because I am slow again.

I think of the Olympic Games. The modern Games began in Athens in 1896, and cycling was one of the sports. We are not Olympic riders, but we are a team. We **have fun riding**, and the day is perfect.
